findings.evidence: The combined-one-fails eval requires that the agent "Leaves the failed source's references and rubric untouched", although its fixture reports a failed recovery and the separate recovery-failed eval requires restoring the references from backup.
findings.fix: Change the combined-failure assertion and expected output to require the backup recovery described by the failure fixture, while still checking that the other fetcher is processed and no unsafe commit occurs.

findings.evidence: For an unspecified source the skill says to "make one commit", while the individual unchanged and repair-only branches say to stop without committing; the same combined instruction also applies when a fetcher fails.
findings.fix: Define combined finalization explicitly: make no commit when both sources are unchanged; preserve the repair-only pending-commit policy; on either failure, report and recover as appropriate and do not commit an inconsistent refresh. Commit once only when the eligible changes and checks have succeeded.

findings.evidence: For a broken source anchor, the reference says to resume at Source 1 step 3; when the fetcher reports no changed or removed pages and rubric_stale is false, that step selects the no-rubric-edit repair branch instead of fixing the anchor.
findings.fix: Add an explicit anchor-only branch that identifies the renamed or missing heading, updates the rubric source anchor and affected criteria as needed, and reruns rubric-check; do not route it through the no-rubric-edit branch.

findings.evidence: The Claude Code workflow runs fetch-claude-specs.sh without stating its Bash 4.4+, Git 2.36+, and GNU realpath requirements; those prerequisites are only in README.md, which the workflow does not instruct the agent to read.
findings.fix: State the Claude fetcher's prerequisites in the workflow or direct the agent to the prerequisite paragraph in README.md before running it, with a stop-and-report fallback when they are unavailable.

findings.evidence: Step 3.2 says "rubric_stale false (so changed or removed is non-empty: references repaired or pruned to the pin the rubric already matches)". The fetcher advances the pin whenever changed is non-empty ("[ ${#CHANGED[@]} -gt 0 ] && PINNED=$RESOLVED") and sets rubric_stale only by comparing the rubric spec_sha with that new pin, so a content change and rubric_stale false cannot occur together. The gotcha at line 73 states the opposite and is the branch an agent will actually meet.
findings.fix: Rewrite step 3.2 to the case the gotcha already names: changed non-empty and rubric_stale false cannot happen, because any changed file moves sha to resolved and makes rubric_stale true. Keep removed non-empty with rubric_stale false as the only repair-or-prune, no-rule-change branch, and send every changed run down the BASE-diff path.

findings.evidence: Source 2 step 1 stops the whole skill when changed and profiles_stale are empty ("delete the kept directory, report 'Claude Code specs unchanged', edit nothing, stop"), while the intro says a request with no source named runs both fetchers and, if one exits 1, still runs the other.
findings.fix: Change that stop to "stop this source": delete kept, report Claude Code specs unchanged, edit nothing for this source, then return to the caller so an unnamed request can still finish the other source, run build_plugins.py and rubric-check once, and make one commit.

findings.evidence: The only load trigger is "Read this only when fetch-spec.sh reports structure_changed: true or rubric-check reports a broken source anchor." It does not name the reference to leave unread on the ordinary unchanged, repair and rule-update paths.
findings.fix: Add one line at that trigger: do not load references/structure-change.md when structure_changed is false and rubric-check reports no broken source anchor, including the unchanged early return, the repair branch and the rule-update branch.

findings.evidence: 19 queries: 10 should-trigger and 9 should-not-trigger. The near-miss negatives cover judging, validating and summarizing, but none names the repo's other vendored docs or another host's format rules.
findings.fix: Add one should-not-trigger near-miss such as "refresh the opencode plugin format docs we pin" (the body says other hosts are not pinned) so the set reaches about 20 and tests the Claude Code boundary.

findings.evidence: Step 2 says the unchanged early return is "changed empty AND removed empty AND rubric_stale false". The eval fixture fetch-unchanged.json is exactly that case and omits removed, structure_changed, new_pages and removed_pages, all of which the fetcher always prints. An agent that treats a missing removed as not empty never takes the early return the eval requires.
findings.fix: State the test in terms of the arrays the fetcher always emits: unchanged only when changed and removed are both present and empty and rubric_stale is false; a missing field is a malformed result, so re-run with -h and do not guess. Put the same four fields in evals/files/fetch-unchanged.json and the other fetcher fixtures.

findings.evidence: Source 2 step 4 says a rule change updates "the provenance header (digest lines and the '<page>: <bytes> bytes, sha256 <hash>' lines)". fetch-claude-specs.sh records only url and sha256 per page in SOURCE.json and never a byte count, and it deletes the kept pages unless --keep is still holding them. The byte lines in docs/audit/artifact-specs.md (lines 5-7) therefore have no source the workflow names.
findings.fix: Tell the agent to set each provenance byte line from the kept page before deleting it, with wc -c on "$kept/<page>.md", and to set the sha256 from SOURCE.json pages[page].sha256. Name that command next to the digest-line update so the header rubric-check reads can actually be produced.

findings.evidence: `PNG=$(bash "$PRD" render path/to/diagram.drawio | jq -r '.[0].png')` ... `Exit 1 means no PNG`
findings.fix: Capture and check the render command's exit status before piping its JSON to jq, or enable and check pipefail explicitly. On failure, report stderr and use the fallback body without attempting an attachment.

findings.evidence: `git rev-list --merges "origin/$BASE..origin/$HEAD"`. Empty output means the history was squashed or rebased ... stop and ask for an explicit merged source PR.
findings.fix: Do not treat the presence of any merge commit as proof that all relevant promotions used merge commits: mixed merge, squash and rebase histories can pass this check while returning already-promoted sources. Require explicit source PRs when the merge strategy cannot be verified, or verify candidate PRs against a reliable promotion boundary.

findings.evidence: `for f in "$@"` copies each destination before checking the next destination for a symlink; SKILL.md says `render` exit 1 means no PNG was copied.
findings.fix: Preflight all destination paths and stage all copies before replacing any output, with rollback or another all-or-nothing strategy for replacement failures. Add a multi-input test where a later destination is a symlink or cannot be written, and ensure the documented failure contract matches the implementation.

findings.evidence: repo prints <owner>/<repo> parsed from origin (https, git@github.com: and ssh://, optional .git or trailing slash); a non-github.com or unparsable origin exits 1 naming the URL
findings.fix: The model already parses those remote forms. Keep only the non-obvious part: on a non-github.com host repo exits 1 and the caller must set REPO=<host>/<owner>/<repo>. Move the URL-form list to references/ if a user asks for it, or record the deletion in docs/audit/recovery/pr-diagrams/record.md.

findings.evidence: The publish URL is the absolute form ... the absolute form and GHE are unverified: after the edit, open the PR and check that the image renders.
findings.fix: Keep the unverified-absolute-form warning, and add the non-obvious consequence: a private repo or GHE can show a broken image even when the blob URL is correct, so the check is part of publish success, not optional confirmation.

findings.evidence: Use when attaching or hosting a diagram image in a PR body, choosing where diagram images live, reusing diagrams in a promotion PR, finding related merged PRs, or reusing reviewers from merged source PRs
findings.fix: Render draw.io diagrams to PNGs with the diagram embedded, attach them to a pull request with gh --attach or, on GitHub Enterprise or gh older than 2.101, publish them to the single pr-diagrams branch, find the merged PRs a promotion should reuse, and collect those source PRs' human reviewers for the promotion. Use when attaching or hosting a diagram image in a PR body, choosing where diagram images live, reusing diagrams in a promotion PR, finding related merged PRs, or reusing reviewers from merged source PRs, even without the words "pr-diagrams" or "draw.io", including a request to create a per-PR image branch. Not for drawing a diagram of a module, creating a pull request, listing the reviewers already requested on a PR (gh pr view), converting a .drawio to a PNG for slides, or editing draw.io XML (draw-io).

findings.evidence: Loaded on demand by the explain-pr-changes command, and by the skill's SKILL.md for the two sections it names.
findings.fix: In SKILL.md Reference, name the two headings an agent must not load for the skill's own workflow, None-mode diagram filter and Body templates, next to the existing Do NOT load sentence, so the command-owned blocks are not pulled in with the two gated sections.

findings.evidence: On that warning take the branch route (publish) for that PNG instead of --attach.
findings.fix: State the default as one route for the whole body: if any rendered PNG warns that it is over 10 MB, publish every image for that PR through branch mode and do not mix --attach with publish URLs in the same body, unless the user explicitly asks to attach only the files under the limit.

findings.evidence: Twelve evals cover attach, render, related, reviewers, branch naming and recovery, but none assert the merge-commit stop in Promotion step 3 or the gh-and-origin repository mismatch that makes publish exit 2.
findings.fix: Add one eval whose prompt shows empty git rev-list --merges output and asserts the agent stops and asks for --reuse-from rather than reusing the related list, and one whose prompt shows publish exit 2 naming two different repositories and asserts no retry and no hand-built push.

findings.evidence: Should-not-trigger queries include draw a diagram, create a pull request, edit mxGraph XML, convert to a PNG for slides, explain the PR, add Mermaid to the README, list requested reviewers and push a feature branch.
findings.fix: Add near-misses that share the skill's objects but need a neighbor: comment an existing diagram image on a PR without attaching one, and request reviewers on a promotion PR without collecting them from its source PRs.

findings.evidence: A standalone caller sets these once; the explain-pr-changes command sets its own: AD, REPO, BASE, HEAD, TITLE.
findings.fix: Tell the standalone caller to set and export AD, REPO, BASE, HEAD and TITLE before any later step, and say that references/pr-body.md reads those names. Without them the branch-recovery and title-assembly blocks have unset variables.

findings.evidence: Loaded from SKILL.md without the command: ... and the $AD/state.env appends belong to the command; skip them.
findings.fix: Replace the command-only state.env sentences in the standalone path with the skill's own recovery: quote gh and publish stderr in the final message, and do not tell a standalone caller to continue to reviewers or append N to a file the skill never creates.

findings.evidence: The moved-path eval expects "Reports the status path-moved" and a track command, but its fixture supplies no candidate content review; the contents-404-moved eval has the same gap.
findings.fix: Add candidate content and a verifiable review result to both fixtures, assert classification before tracking, and add an unresolved-content case that expects no track call.

findings.evidence: The tree command filters the response to '.tree[] | .path', but the next checkpoint requires checking the response's 'truncated' flag.
findings.fix: Preserve and inspect the full tree response, including truncated, before listing candidates; do not treat an incomplete tree as proof that a path is missing.

findings.evidence: The compare command filters the response to selected patches, yet the procedure requires detecting a 300-file response and the compare commit limit before tracking.
findings.fix: Preserve the compare response metadata and complete file list before filtering patches; detect file and commit truncation, paginate or otherwise retrieve the complete changes, and leave the artifact unresolved if completeness cannot be established.

findings.evidence: For several candidate paths, the procedure says 'record no path-moved' but does not prohibit tracking sibling rows; each track call stamps last_reviewed on all sibling rows.
findings.fix: Treat an unresolved multi-candidate relocation as an artifact-wide no-track condition until the user selects a candidate and its content review is complete, preserving the other rows' fallback review dates.

findings.evidence: The contents test relies on the version-sensitive 'gh api --silent' flag; the README links the GitHub CLI manual but gives no date checked, and the procedure does not read the flag live.
findings.fix: Instruct the agent to check the installed gh api --help for the flag before use, or cite the official gh api manual alongside the flag with the date checked.

findings.evidence: **Claude Code:** `cp -r skills/skill-updater ~/.claude/skills/` and **claude.ai:** add the skill to project knowledge, or paste `SKILL.md` into the conversation.
findings.fix: The model already knows how to install a skill directory. Move the Install section to references/install.md only if users ask for it by name; otherwise delete it and add a para row to docs/audit/recovery/skill-updater/record.md. Keep the Sources credit.

findings.evidence: registry-current expected output records current from stale false and error null, but its assertion also requires inspecting upstream content, and registry-kept-new-path does the same.
findings.fix: Rewrite both expected_output texts so they require the step-4 content read (and, for a row with last_upstream_sha, the compare) before status current, matching the assertions.

findings.evidence: A credit line naming an upstream with no row: propose the row in updates.md ... and give no track call at all.
findings.fix: Change step 2 so a credit with no matching row still runs step 6 and records each existing row, including a source-less local row, and only withholds track for the missing source row it proposes.
